title: Working at Redwood — Handbook and Onboarding Overview
author: Avery Chen
content:
Overview

This document is Redwood Inference’s canonical company handbook for employees and candidates. It covers: working culture and expectations, role levels and career ladders, benefits and perks, hiring and onboarding overview, and practical internal tools & access procedures. Use this as the first reference for new hires and managers; detailed team-level variants may exist in team wikis.

Section 1 — Culture and working at Redwood

Introduction
- Our mission: Make high-performance, reliable LLM inference accessible to every engineering team.
- We are engineering-first, shipment-oriented, and customer-focused. Our values are:
  - Ownership: ship and operate what you build.
  - Clarity: clear APIs, clear docs, clear communication.
  - Reliability: design for production and graceful degradation.
  - Continuous learning: measure, iterate, and share learnings.

Work model and expectations
- Work model: hybrid by default. Core collaboration days are Tuesday and Thursday. Teams may set different core days with manager approval.
- Hours and availability: flexible working hours; expected overlap with 10:00–16:00 local time for collaboration. Document your working hours in your profile.
- Time off: flexible PTO policy (see Section 3) — request via HR portal and notify your manager.
- Communication norms: async-first in docs and PRs; Slack for urgent matters. Use concise status updates on team channels; use threads to keep channels focused.

Psychological safety and inclusion
- Redwood is committed to inclusive hiring and a harassment-free workplace. Report concerns to People Ops or via the anonymous reporting channel. We run regular ERG and inclusion trainings.

Section 2 — Roles, levels, and career ladders

High-level leveling
- IC ladder (engineering/product/experts): L3 (Associate) -> L4 (Mid) -> L5 (Senior) -> L6 (Staff) -> L7 (Principal).
- Manager ladder: M1 (Manager) -> M2 (Senior Manager) -> M3 (Director) and above.

Expectations by level (summary)
- L3: Delivers assigned tasks with guidance; learns codebase and processes.
- L4: Owns medium-sized features end-to-end; participates in design and code reviews.
- L5: Leads cross-team features; coaches others; influences roadmap.
- L6+: Technical leadership for the org; defines system-level architecture and mentoring programs.

Promotion and calibration process
1. Promotion nomination by manager (packet includes impact examples, 3-5 artifacts: PRs, design docs, customer incidents).
2. Peer reviews and manager calibration panel.
3. Compensation review and final sign-off by People Ops.
4. Typical cadence: twice yearly calibration cycles, with off-cycle promotions for exceptional cases.

Manager responsibilities
- 1:1s weekly, career planning, performance feedback, and onboarding new hires. Prepare promotion packets and run calibration-ready reviews.

Section 3 — Benefits and perks (summary)

Health and financial
- Medical, dental, vision plans with company contribution (US, EU localized plans). Details in benefits portal.
- 401(k) with employer match (US); pension/retirement guidance for other regions.
- Equity: standard RSU/options grants with refresh cycles for sustained contributors.

Leave policies
- Flexible PTO (manager-approved, trust-based).
- Parental leave: 18 weeks primary caregiver, 8 weeks secondary caregiver (global equivalents may vary).
- Bereavement, jury duty, and short-term disability per regional regulations.

Wellness and development
- Stipends: home office setup ($500 one-time), wellness allowance ($200/year), learning & conference budget ($1,500/year for most roles).
- Mental health: EAP and counseling sessions covered.
- Commuter benefits or mobility stipend depending on region.

Perks and discounts
- Free access to premium learning platforms, team offsites budget, referral bonus program, and monthly team social budgets.

How to enroll and manage benefits
- Use the benefits portal (link in People Ops Confluence page) for plan elections, claims, and reimbursements. Open enrollment occurs annually in November. For immediate questions, contact benefits@redwood.ai.

Section 4 — Hiring and onboarding overview

Hiring process (standard flow)
1. Role posted and recruiter screen.
2. Hiring manager technical/role screen.
3. Interview loop (4–6 interviews): technical take-home or system design + collaboration exercises + bar-raiser.
4. Hiring committee review and offer approval.
5. Offer, background check, and I-9/visa paperwork (as applicable).

Interview guidelines and candidate experience
- Interviewers must use structured rubrics and provide written feedback within 48 hours. Focus on job-relevant skills, collaboration, and problem-solving. Avoid asking questions about protected characteristics.

Offer and negotiation
- Compensation is set based on level, market data, and internal equity. Recruiters will present base, equity, and benefits. Counter-offers are handled by recruiting and People Ops.

Onboarding plan (first 90 days)
- Pre-boarding: account provisioning, welcome packet, manager sets first-week goals.
- Day 0 / 1 checklist: HR orientation, security training, laptop & access, team meet-and-greet, set Slack status and calendar.
- Week 1: read team docs, small starter task, pair programming sessions, 1:1 with manager to set 30/60/90.
- Month 1: deliver first small feature or operational task, complete required compliance trainings, update onboarding doc.
- Month 2–3: take ownership of a medium feature, present a 90-day learnings demo, discuss career goals and next milestones with manager.

Manager onboarding checklist (new manager)
- Complete manager training (People Ops), set team goals, schedule skip-levels, and review direct reports’ career plans.

Section 5 — Internal tools and access guides

Core systems (what to use and primary owners)
- Communication: Slack (default channels #all, #engineering, team channels). Owner: Eng DX.
- Docs & knowledge: Confluence (this handbook), team pages. Owner: People Ops + Eng DX.
- Source control: GitHub (private org). Owner: Eng Infra.
- Project tracking: Linear (or Jira for specific teams). Owner: Eng PM.
- CI/CD: Buildkite and internal pipelines. Owner: Eng Infra.
- Observability: Datadog for infra metrics, Sentry for errors. Owner: Eng SRE.
- Identity & access: Okta + SCIM for provisioning. Owner: Security.
- Passwords & secrets: 1Password + KMS for production secrets. Owner: Security.
- HR & payroll: Gusto (US) / Deel / Local payroll partners. Owner: People Ops.

Requesting access (how-to)
1. Submit an access request in the IT ticketing system (link on People Ops page). Include: tool name, justification, requester manager, and required role.
2. Manager approves via ticket.
3. Provisioning owner grants access and documents MFA setup.
4. Confirm access in first-week checklist.

Security requirements and MFA
- MFA is mandatory for all accounts. Use Okta Verify or YubiKey for production access. Device encryption and approved OS versions required for remote work.

Knowledge sharing and documentation standards
- Use Confluence for design docs and runbooks. Include owner, date, TL;DR, background, decision, and action items in every doc. Use the internal ADR template for architecture decisions.

Section 6 — Manager and people-op playbooks (quick reference)

New hire launch (manager steps)
1. Prepare first-week schedule and starter tasks.
2. Ensure laptop & access complete 48 hours before start.
3. Introduce to team, schedule 1:1 weekly, set 30/60/90 goals.

Performance reviews and calibration
- Cadence: annual performance review with mid-year check-in. Manager writes initial summary; peers provide feedback. People Ops runs calibration to ensure fairness.

Handling escalations
- Use the escalation playbook (see Confluence page) for customer incidents, HR issues, and security breaches. Notify People Ops and Eng SRE as appropriate.

Section 7 — FAQ and quick links

FAQ
- Who do I talk to about benefits? People Ops (benefits@redwood.ai).
- How do I request time off? Use the HR portal and update your manager.
- Where are team runbooks? Confluence -> eng-platform -> runbooks.

Quick links (internal)
- New hire checklist: /confluence/company-handbook/new-hire-checklist
- Benefits portal: /confluence/company-handbook/benefits-portal
- Access request form: /confluence/policies-and-process/access-request
- Interview rubric: /confluence/company-handbook/interview-rubric

Appendix — contact points
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.ai
- IT/Ticketing: it-support@redwood.ai
- Security: security@redwood.ai
- Recruiting: recruiting@redwood.ai

Document maintenance
- Owner: People Ops. Review cadence: annual or when policies change. For corrections, submit an edit request in Confluence and notify the document owner.

End of handbook summary.
